review_reason: The task explicitly calls out 'unvalidated math notation detection' as a named weak spot. This fixture reveals a concrete, specific way that detection can fail: Wikipedia chemistry articles represent chemical formulas using plain HTML <sub>/<sup> tags (e.g. C<sub>9</sub>H<sub>8</sub>O<sub>4</sub>), NOT LaTeX delimiters or MathML <math> tags (verified: zero <math> tags and zero 'mwe-math' rendered-image classes anywhere in this document). Any math-detector keyed specifically to LaTeX ($...$, \(...\)) or MathML will completely miss this chemical notation. This must not be rubber-stamped either way (present or absent) without a human confirming which behavior Pith actually intends.

math_notes: Chemical notation is present via HTML <sub>/<sup> tags only (3 <sub> + 2 <sup> occurrences confirmed directly in this excerpt): the molecular formula C9H8O4 (rendered as C<sub>9</sub>H<sub>8</sub>O<sub>4</sub>) inside the infobox, and unit exponents like 'g·mol<sup>−1</sup>' and 'g/cm<sup>3</sup>'. There is NO LaTeX and NO MathML anywhere in this document (confirmed: zero <math> tags, zero 'mwe-math' classes). This is a fundamentally different representation of 'math-like' content than fixtures 01/02 (LaTeX PDF equations) and is exactly the kind of notation the task's 'unvalidated math notation detection' weak spot is worried about missing.

notes_for_implementer: Central question for this fixture: does Pith's math-notation detector recognize chemical formulas expressed via nested <sub>/<sup> tags (C9H8O4) as 'math-like content', or does it only fire on LaTeX/MathML? Neither answer is obviously wrong, but it must be a deliberate design decision, not an accident of the detector only having been tested against LaTeX -- hence needs_human_review. Separately, note the corrected understanding that current Wikipedia chemistry infoboxes use class='infobox' generically, NOT a distinct 'chembox' class as commonly assumed from older Wikipedia HTML dumps -- any Pith logic hardcoded to look for a literal 'chembox' class string would fail to recognize this infobox at all.
